transcript.t: Objective reactions design process to design software again. Migratory winger. Principal research scientist with Autodesk Research. My colleague Brian Lee helped put together this presentation but unfortunately wasn't able to attend this year, so I'm going to try to investigate.
transcript.tr: 客观反应设计过程来再次设计软件。迁徙边锋。 Autodesk Research 首席研究科学家。我的同事 Brian Lee 帮助整理了这个演示文稿，但不幸的是今年无法参加，所以我将尝试进行调查。

transcript.t: Just to set some context in this talk, I'm going to provide first a kind of overview and kind of high level context of the vision of our research. And the second part, we'll share some demos of project assistant research, which is also on the Exhibit 4. So I encourage you all to visit. We'll then discuss how these ideas can kind of address key critical moments in AC workflows. And finally, I want to share some kind of thoughts and hypothesis on, you know, how we can prepare ourselves.
transcript.tr: 为了在这次演讲中设置一些背景，我将首先提供我们研究愿景的一种概述和一种高级背景。第二部分，我们将分享一些项目助理研究的演示，这也在附件4中。所以我鼓励大家参观。然后我们将讨论这些想法如何解决 AC 工作流程中的关键时刻。最后，我想分享一些关于我们如何做好准备的想法和假设。

transcript.t: Before we start, I kind of want to stay with a little bit of a fabrication. So imagine that soon in the future there no longer will be a kind of distinction between your design process and the software that you use. So what does this mean?
transcript.tr: 在我们开始之前，我想先做一些捏造的事情。因此，想象一下，在不久的将来，您的设计过程和您使用的软件之间将不再存在某种区别。那么这意味着什么呢？

transcript.t: When you started the AC project, every building, every new renovation will not only result in a new physical built artifact, but also a new piece of software that will become a starting point for your next project.
transcript.tr: 当您开始 AC 项目时，每栋建筑、每一次新的翻修不仅会产生一个新的物理建筑工件，而且还会产生一个新的软件，它将成为您下一个项目的起点。

transcript.t: The future, how you work and the data you have and use will start to drive the software experience that you use to create your your products.
transcript.tr: 未来，您的工作方式以及您拥有和使用的数据将开始推动您用于创建产品的软件体验。
